sentences.text: The prosecution case, in brief, is this that a report was lodged by the father of prosecutrix on 29.08.2014 at Police Station, Chhura alleging therein that on 27.08.2014 at about 09:00 PM, the appellant abducted the prosecutrix from her lawful guardianship and detained her in his house and during course of detention, committed sexual intercourse with her.

Based upon the said report, FIR bearing crime No. 96/2014 was registered against the appellant and on completion of investigation,
final report/charge sheet was filed against appellant for the offence under Sections 363, 366(d),
376(z<)of IPC and 4 & 6 of POCSO Act.
4. Prosecution in order to prove its case examined total 16 witnesses.
Statements of appellant (accused) was also recorded under Section 313 of CrPC in which he denied all incriminating evidence appearing against him, pleaded innocence and false implication.
However, no defence witness has been examined in his defence.

5. After hearing counsel for the parties and appreciating evidence available on record, the trial Court vide impugned judgment dated 06.03.2020 convicted and sentenced the accused/ appellant in the manner as described above of this judgment.
Hence this appeal.

6. Learned counsel for appellant submits that as per prosecution story, age of the prosecutrix was 17 years at the time of alleged incident, but no authentic documentary proof was filed in order to show that the prosecutrix was a minor girl on the alleged date, even she has almost a major lady.

Further,
PW-2/father of prosecutrix has categorically admitted in his deposition that he does not know the exact date of birth of the prosecutrix and he stated that she would be 17 years old, and my daughter must have completed 18 years of age and thereafter he stated that earlier he said, her age is 16 years.
7. Learned Counsel appearing for the appellant submits that she went alongwith his house and no alarm was raised by her.
Both of them established physical relationship with their own will.

Conduct of prosecutrix is seen in its entirety, it is clear that she had been a consenting party to the act of the appellant having developed an intimacy with him and nowhere she appears to have resisted while making physical relation.

8. Learned counsel further submits that trial Court convicted the appellant relied upon the statement of PW-1/victim, but her statement is not reliable as there are many contradictions,
omissions and development in her statement, which was not considered properly by the learned trial court.

From the statements of the prosecutrix recorded before the police, Magistrate and the Court it reflects that she is not a reliable witness and appears to be a consenting party to the act of appellant.

sentences.text: Trial Court also ignored the fact that nothing has been found in the medical report of victim though there is allegation that appellant has established forceful physical relationship with her on many occasion.
Medical evidence also shows that there was no sign of forcible sexual intercourse on the body of the prosecutrix.
The prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt against the appellant and therefore, the appellant deserves to be acquitted of all the charges.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State supporting the impugned judgment and submits that the prosecutrix was a minor girl aged about 16 years on the date of incident and this fact has been duly proved by the prosecution by adducing Kotwari Panji and conducting Ossification Test.
The act committed by the appellant makes him liable for conviction under Sections 363 and 366 of IPC and under Section 8 of POSCO.
Being so, the impugned judgment is strictly in accordance with law and the present appeal is liable to be dismissed.

10. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the recorded placed on record.
11.
In order to consider the age of prosecutrix, this Court has to examine the evidence/material placed on record by the prosecution.

The prosecution has mainly relied upon Kotwari Panji (Ex.P-21 & 21C) produced by the Kotwar Ramkumar (PW- 11) wherein the date of birth of the prosecutrix is mentioned as 29.11.1997 and which was registered on 15.12.1997.
Further Kotwar Ramkumar stated in his deposition that on the information given by the father of victim, he has registered her date of birth.
The detail in the Kotwari Panji was recorded after 15 days of the mentioned date of birth of the victim.
Further, with respect to determine the date of birth of the victim, ossification test was conducted by the prosecution, in which also the age of the victim was said to be around 16 years.
In rebuttal to the said documentary evidence, no such evidence has been presented by the appellant side, which could refute the fact of the date of birth mentioned in the said documents.

Therefore, this Court finds that legally admissible evidence has been brought by the prosecution to prove the fact that at the time of alleged incident, her age was 16 years which is less than 18 years and she was undoubtedly minor on the date of incident.

12. Prosecutrix (PW-1) has categorically stated that on the date of incident when she was attending nature's call, at that time accused/appellant came from her backside, gagged her mouth and said that he would marry her and took her towards his house with intent to commit rape on her.
Further she stated that she told to the Police that the accused had taken me to his room and raped me thrice.

13. Thus, in view of the fact that the prosecutrix at the time of incident was a minor, the appellant-accused does not get any advantage even if the case of the appellant is accepted to be a case of consent as the consent of a minor would not be of any relevance.

As such, it cannot be said that the prosecution has not been successful in establishing the guilt of the appellant beyond the shadow of reasonable doubt in respect of the offence punishable under Section 363, 366 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act and, in the circumstances, the trial Court has not committed any manifest error of law and fact in convicting the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 363 & 366 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act, which deserves to be and is hereby affirmed and maintained.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that in the year 2014 punishment for offence under Section 4 of the POSCO Act was from 07 years upto RI for life imprisonment.

As per amendment dated 16.08.2019,
punishment for offence under Section 4 of the POSCO Act has been substituted and thereby punishment shall not be less than 10 years upto RI for life.

15. With regard to the sentence in the instant case, incident took place on 29.08.2014, hence, the trial Court ought to have been convicted and sentenced the appellant as per punishment prevailing in the year 2014 for the offence under Section 4 of the POSCO Act, ie from 07 years upto RI for life imprisonment.
Considering the aforesaid fact, this Court is of the opinion that it would be in the interest of justice, the sentence imposed upon him i.e. 10 years is reduced to rigorous imprisonment for 7 years.
However, fine imposed by trial Court is maintained.
16. The appellant is in jail and he shall serve out the sentence as modified above.
17. With the aforesaid observations, the criminal appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove.
18. Let a copy of this order and the original records be transmitted to the trial court concerned forthwith for necessary information and compliance.
